### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49c8e0f069ac5e21b11ba40d8bbbbfd8cd2eced2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `da2e1e22528bc1acd85309b8c0637ef815d9f87c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .github/workflows/ci.yml + packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-37095-pgvector-extension.test.ts

Inputs read: card #37095 (body and all five comments, rulings 7146141300 and 7146156389 included), PR #37155 (body, both comments, two-file net diff against main), the 58 check-runs on the head (44 success, 14 skipped, 0 failure, 0 pending), and the cited code on the branch tree. One registry read: `GET mirror.gcr.io/v2/pgvector/pgvector/manifests/0.8.7-pg16` answered 200 with index digest `sha256:484e838076e04939d27d3e176e91c86eea96236126023be8d3059761122e579f`, the digest the ci.yml comment records.

### ① Derived judgments

**Which events run `temporal-conformance`** (new `if:`: `!cancelled() && core != 'false' && event != 'pull_request' && (event != 'merge_group' || temporal_live != 'false')`):

| event | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| push to main | runs when `core` hit | unchanged (`temporal_live` is not read) |
| schedule / workflow_dispatch | runs (`core` falls to 'true') | unchanged |
| merge_group, diff hits `temporal_live` | skipped | **runs** |
| merge_group, diff misses | skipped | skipped (publishes a `skipped` check-run) |
| merge_group, filter step or job failed | skipped | **runs** (output '' reads 'true'; a dead `filter` job reads '' which is not 'false') |
| pull_request | skipped | skipped; observed on this head (`Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`: skipped) |

- This is ruling B as worded: queue run on path hits, `pull_request` still excluded, #22998 revised for this one job. `dogfood-verify` and `ui-published-artifacts` keep the two-term deny-list.
- **Fail-open is the right default.** It is THE FILTER CONTRACT's half 1 and the same spelling the ui outputs use on the queue. The failure direction is one extra ~9-minute run on an entry, never a hit that silently skipped.
- **`core != 'false'` on merge_group** is still in the expression and is inert there (`core` is forced 'true'), so `temporal_live` alone decides on the queue. Every `temporal_live` path is also a `core` path (`packages/**`, `ci.yml`), so the push run that follows a queue hit also runs the job. A hit therefore runs twice (queue, then push): `MAIN_ONLY_JOBS` in `scripts/ci/scheduled-full-run.mjs` forbids this job from borrowing the queue verdict. The added minutes are purely additive, as the PR body says.
- **Image.** `pgvector/pgvector:0.8.7-pg16` is built on the official PG 16 Debian image: same major, same entrypoint and `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` contract, `pg_isready` and `psql` present, so the health command, the `ALTER SYSTEM SET timezone` step and the four legs that take `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` (driver-sql, the non-SQL leg's service-analytics cells, metadata-protocol live files, runtime cascade-delete) see the same server surface. The PG minor is whatever the pgvector build carried; nothing in the job pins a minor. None of this has run in CI: on this head the job is skipped.
- **Pin convention.** The only other service image in `.github/workflows/` is `mirror.gcr.io/library/mysql:8.0`, a moving tag; no workflow pins an image digest. An exact tag is stricter than the neighbour and within convention. The digest in the comment is a record, not an enforcement (nit: `tag@sha256:…` is accepted by `services.*.image` and would enforce it; this is a third-party image, not Docker `library/`).
- **Required set: unchanged, and that is the finding.** `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` is NOT a required context: `scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs` holds it as a tombstone (#22998) and AGENTS.md lists eleven blocking contexts without it. The merge queue enforces only the required set, so a red `temporal-conformance` on a queue build is advisory and the entry lands. This PR adds no `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` row (correctly: ruling B did not rule enrolment; the dogfood precedent needed its own letter, record 6669982756).

S1 (should-fix) — The PR body's 维护者速读 (「只会让这项检查变红、挡住相关合并」) and the dev's final-head comment 7147713376 ("a red there ejects the PR") state a consequence the diff does not have. The context is outside the required set, so a red queue run of this job ejects nothing: the entry merges and the red arrives on `main` (push and 4-hourly runs, and the release lane's full-battery read). Correct both texts to "advisory on the queue", and put the enrolment question (re-add the context to the ruleset plus a `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` row, as #30461 did for dogfood) to the maintainer as its own ruling. Do not decide it in this PR.

S1 (should-fix) — Rule text for #22998 is left stating the pre-ruling rule in the file the PR edits. `ci.yml` THE TWO SPEEDS header (lines 130-137) still says `temporal-conformance` spells both `!= 'pull_request' && != 'merge_group'`; the `filter.outputs` comment (lines 332-345) still says only the three ui outputs read the step on merge_group and that `core` is read "on push / schedule" by this job; the step comment (line 454) still says `merge_group` joined the allow-list "for the ui outputs alone". Outside the diff, read not reviewed: `docs/agents/multi-agent-discipline.md:138` ("Temporal Conformance ... stay full-battery only") and the tombstone prose in `scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs` say the same. Revise the in-file text in this PR and name the two outside surfaces in the hand-off.

S1 (should-fix) — The `temporal_live` list misses files the job itself selects, against ruling B's "the job's own test files". (a) `packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/live-mysql-database.isolation.test.ts`: the step's `live-mysql` substring selects it (the ci.yml comment counts three `live-mysql*` files), and the glob `*.live-mysql.test.ts` does not match it. (b) The 22 `packages/services/service-analytics` test files that key live cells on `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` (#21564): this job's non-SQL leg is the only place they run against a server, and it is the new image they run against. Measured on the local history (2026-11-14 to 2026-11-24, 1689 first-parent commits): the PR's list hits 43 commits; adding those 22 files makes 51 (+19%); adding the whole package makes 74. Add (a) and the 22 files (or a glob for them), or record in the PR body why they stay out. The rest of the list is minimal and matches the ruling; leaving out core, formula, driver-memory and driver-mongodb is reasoned and accepted.

Note for #37100, no finding here: `packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/**` starts the job, but no step runs that package's tests until #37100 adds one (a governed `ci.yml` edit of its own).

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` holds. The diff is a workflow file and one `*.test.ts` under `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/`; that package publishes `dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` only, so nothing published changes. `skip-changeset` is correct and `Check Changeset` is success on the head. No spec, schema or runtime surface is touched.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev ordering deviation** (second push before the overlap-check and the derived gates; both rerun afterwards, clean): accepted. The rerun is on the reviewed head, `mergeable_state` is clean, and the head's check-runs show no failure. No finding.
- `open_questions`: none in the dev report. Out-of-scope doc drift (`integration-system.json`, ADR-0104 still say `postgres:16`) is named in the PR body; accepted as noted, not filed.
- **First live run happens only in the queue.**

S1 (should-fix) — Run the job once on the PR branch before the hand-merge: one operator `workflow_dispatch` of `ci.yml` on `claude/issue-37095-ci-pgvector`, read `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` green with `sql-driver-37095-pgvector-extension.test.ts (2 tests)` in the driver-sql step. Reason: per ①, the queue run is advisory, so there is no ejection backstop. A defective image, a failed pull through the mirror, or a 0.8.7 behaviour the local 0.6.0 run did not show would land and turn every later push and scheduled run of `main` red, which blocks the release lane's full-battery read. The maintainer rejected option A as the standing path; a one-off pre-check of a governed image swap is a different thing and costs one full-battery run. If the maintainer declines it, the two-minute check in the PR body must be read on the queue run before the entry lands, and a red there is a revert.

- SQL push-down check: not applicable. The diff adds no id materialisation and no in-app join; the test's ordering is done by the server (`ORDER BY` on the L2 operator, `LIMIT 2`).

### ④ Design judgment

**`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** against ruling 7146156389 and the code it cites: the `if:` and the filter output agree with the ruling and with THE FILTER CONTRACT (both halves: `|| 'true'` on the output, `!= 'false'` at the reader). The filter rides the existing `dorny/paths-filter` step, which already runs on merge_group with `continue-on-error`, so no new step, permission or action is introduced. The path globs were checked against the tree: the metadata-protocol and runtime globs match the 9 live files and the one cascade-delete file they are meant to (the gaps are in ① above). `check-expected-skips` reads the new `if:` as the queue-and-full shape (one top-level `!= 'pull_request'` term), so the skip on this PR head is an expected skip. Findings: the three in ①.

**`sql-driver-37095-pgvector-extension.test.ts`** against the card's acceptance and the testkit it uses:
- Gating is the package's own: `declareDialectCell(PG_CELL, …)`, the seam 94 files in `driver-sql/src` go through. Off PG it is a named skip; with `OS_EXPECT_LIVE_DIALECT_MATRIX=1` and no URL it is a named red. The job's driver-sql step sets both the URL and the flag and runs the whole package suite, so the file runs there and cannot skip silently. `Test Core` on the head is green with the file present (named skip).
- It proves what the card asks: `create extension if not exists vector` executes against the server (an image without the extension fails in `beforeAll`), `pg_extension` is read back for exactly one row, a `vector(3)` column is created, and three rows are ordered by L2 distance with ids `[1, 3]` and distances `0`, `1` and `sqrt(26)` asserted. The expected values are exact in float8.
- Isolation is sound: the table lives in the file's own schema (`currentLiveSchema()`), the extension's schema is read back and used to qualify the type and operator instead of assumed, the extension is never dropped by the file, and the globalSetup teardown's `drop schema … cascade` removes it with the schema. No residue reaches the later legs that share the database.
- Limits, stated not graded: it pins presence of the extension, not the 0.8.7 version; and the only run so far is local on pgvector 0.6.0.

**Minutes estimate.** The PR body's 156 hits of 5275 first-parent commits in 30 days (3.0%) at a 541 s median gives about 1,400 runner-minutes (about 23 h). The local clone is shallow (history from 2026-11-14), so only a 10.3-day window could be counted: 43 hits of 1689 commits (2.5%), which scales to about 125 hits and about 1,130 minutes per 30 days. Same order; the estimate is plausible as a lower bound (re-queued entries rerun it). Not reproduced: the body's 49 `ci.yml` commits in 30 days; the local window shows 4 in 10 days. The per-run median on the new image is NOT MEASURED until the first run.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — REWORK · L1 · head `da2e1e22528bc1acd85309b8c0637ef815d9f87c` · 2026-11-24T23:48Z

Requested by zone a4-K (7147713376) for card #37095. Beside the contract review at this head (CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER): PASS with four should-fix — this round's REWORK, except S1's policy half, which goes to the maintainer.

Holds: ruling B (7146156389) as worded — `temporal-conformance` runs on `merge_group` when the diff hits `temporal_live` (fail-open on a failed filter, matching the filter contract), skips on a miss and on `pull_request`, and is unchanged on push, schedule and dispatch; the exact image tag `mirror.gcr.io/pgvector/pgvector:0.8.7-pg16` exists with the recorded digest (same PG major, entrypoint, `pg_isready`); the new test is gated by `declareDialectCell(PG_CELL)` and proves CREATE EXTENSION and distance ordering. skip-changeset, `Clause-②: no`. Check-runs: 44 success, 14 expected skip, 0 failed. The dev's push-before-gates ordering is accepted (gates rerun clean).

S1 (should-fix) — `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` is not a required context (tombstoned in `scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs`, absent from AGENTS.md's list), so a red run in the queue ejects nothing: the PR body's 「挡住相关合并」 and comment 7147713376's "a red there ejects the PR" are wrong. Correct both to what is true: the queue run reports, it does not block. Whether to make the context required is a separate maintainer question — the seat has put it to the maintainer; this PR does not change the required set.
S2 (should-fix) — the #22998 "two speeds" text is now stale in three places: the `ci.yml` TWO SPEEDS header (~130-137), the filter comments (~332-345, ~454), and `docs/agents/multi-agent-discipline.md` ~138 (governed; same Tier H PR). Amend each to name the one exception and cite 7146156389.
S3 (should-fix) — the `temporal_live` path list misses files this job selects: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/live-mysql-database.isolation.test.ts` (the step's `live-mysql` substring picks it) and the service-analytics tests that key live cells on `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL`, which only this job runs against a server. Add them; restate the hit-rate and minutes (about +19% hits).
S4 (should-fix) — the image and the new test have never run in CI (the job skips on the PR; the local run used pgvector 0.6.0). Before the hand-off, an operator `workflow_dispatch` of `ci.yml` on the PR branch, its result linked in the body — a one-off pre-check, not the standing path ruling B rejected as A.

Minutes: the ~1,400/30 days estimate is plausible but only partly reproduced (a shallow local window scales to ~1,130); state the method and the window.

Delta contract review and delta L1 on the new head, then the hand-off.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e6cb50b2549117a8a9cfd7e4c44fc3b6759235df`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .github/workflows/ci.yml + docs/agents/multi-agent-discipline.md, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-37095-pgvector-extension.test.ts

DELTA review from `da2e1e22528bc1acd85309b8c0637ef815d9f87c` (record 7147819716, PASS with four findings that all carried the id S1) to this head. They are numbered here as the seat's L1 7147827756 numbered them: S1 = the PR body said a red queue run ejects the entry; S2 = stale #22998 "two speeds" text; S3 = gaps in the `temporal_live` path list; S4 = no run of the job before the hand-merge.

Inputs read: `git diff da2e1e22528b e6cb50b25491` (one commit, one parent; 2 files, +55/-19: `ci.yml` and `docs/agents/multi-agent-discipline.md`; the test file is unchanged), the PR body and its six comments (7147827756 and 7149072772 included), the 58 check-runs on the head (45 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure, 0 pending; `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` skipped, as expected on `pull_request`), `mergeable_state` clean, draft. One registry read on 2026-11-25: `GET mirror.gcr.io/v2/pgvector/pgvector/manifests/0.8.7-pg16` answered 200 with `sha256:484e838076e04939d27d3e176e91c86eea96236126023be8d3059761122e579f`.

Merge commits: the branch holds none (`git rev-list --merges origin/main..HEAD` is empty; three single-parent commits on merge-base `9c5fb3efdf33`), so there is no merge tree to compare against `git merge-tree --write-tree`.

### ① Derived judgments

S1: closed
- The PR body now says the queue run is advisory in both places (维护者速读 line 3 and "Advisory on the queue" under What changes 2): the context is outside the required set, a red does not eject the entry, the entry lands and the red shows on `main`. It adds no `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` row and names enrolment as a separate maintainer ruling (as #30461 was for dogfood). The dev's earlier comment is corrected by comment 7147832792.

S2: closed
- `ci.yml`, three places, each read on the new head: THE TWO SPEEDS header names `dogfood-verify` and `ui-published-artifacts` as the two-term jobs and `temporal-conformance` as the exception, cites ruling record 7146156389, and states the run is advisory; the `filter.outputs` comment adds `temporal_live` to the outputs that read the step on `merge_group` and says the job reads `temporal_live` there instead of `core`; the paths-filter step comment drops "for the ui outputs alone" and cites 7146156389.
- `docs/agents/multi-agent-discipline.md` (Two speeds paragraph): `Dogfood Verify CLI` and `UI Published Artifacts` stay full-battery only; one exception for Temporal Conformance on a `temporal_live` hit, citing 7146156389, "not a required context, so that run is advisory and a red lands on `main`".
- **Does the doc edit move a rule beyond the ruling? No.** The first half is ruling B as worded. The second half restates a fact that predates this PR (the context is a #22998 tombstone in `scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs`); it grants no agent a new permission, changes no order of work and takes nothing away from the maintainer. The eleven-context list above it is untouched. The template for these paths carries no `Rule-change-verified:` line (no `.claude/**` path in the diff), so none is written here.
- Still stating the old rule, named in the PR body and left on purpose: the tombstone prose in `scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs`. Accepted: it is about the required set, which this PR does not change.

S3: closed
- metadata-protocol: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/**/*live-mysql*` and `…/*live-postgres*` replace the three narrower globs. Against the head's tree they select the 10 files that carry either substring (9 test files, `live-mysql-database.isolation.test.ts` among them, plus the testkit), which is the set the step's `vitest run live-mysql live-postgres` substrings select, plus the testkit those files import.
- service-analytics: 22 files listed by hand. Re-derived with `git grep -l OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL -- packages/services/service-analytics` on the head and on `origin/main`: 22 files both times, and the sorted set is byte-identical to the 22 paths in the filter. No other file in the package names the variable, `OS_TEST_MYSQL_URL`, or a live-dialect helper; the one helper all 22 import (`default-organization.testkit`) is imported by 48 files and holds no PostgreSQL code. The list is complete today.
- **Hand-list or glob.** The only glob available is the whole `__tests__` directory (223 files); the prior round measured the whole package at 74 hits against 51 for the 22 files in the same window, about 45% more runs for files with no live cell. The hand-list is the choice that matches ruling B's "related files" and is accepted. Its cost is drift, which the ci.yml comment and the PR body both state.

N1 (nit) — nothing pins the 22-file list to the grep that produced it, so a new service-analytics file with a live-PostgreSQL cell is missed in silence. The miss costs only the advisory queue run for that merge (the push run that follows still runs the job: every such file is a `core` path). A filename convention such as metadata-protocol's `*.live-postgres.test.ts`, or a small gate comparing the list to the grep, would remove it. Follow-up card; not a reason to move this head.

- **Filter syntax.** The workflow parses as YAML on the new head; the `filters` block parses to 28 single-quoted entries under `temporal_live`, same indentation and quoting as its neighbours; `*live-mysql*` is ordinary picomatch (a leading `*` matches the empty prefix, so `live-mysql-database.*` is selected). The output line (`steps.changes.outputs.temporal_live || 'true'`) and the job's `if:` are unchanged from the reviewed head. The `filter` job and every lint gate are green on this head.
- **Image pin.** `image: mirror.gcr.io/pgvector/pgvector:0.8.7-pg16@sha256:484e838076e04939d27d3e176e91c86eea96236126023be8d3059761122e579f`. The digest is character-for-character the one record 7147819716 read from the registry, and the tag still resolves to it today. This takes up the prior record's nit; `services.*.image` accepts `tag@digest` and Docker then pulls by digest. `readWorkflowDiff` already reads this PR as Tier H by content, so the pin changes no tier.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from record 7147819716: `Clause-②: no` holds. The delta touches a workflow file and an agent doc; nothing published moves. `skip-changeset` stands (`Check Changeset` reads skipped on this head under the label).

### ③ Boundary flags

S4: closed
- Closed as a review finding only: no diff can satisfy it, and the dev routed it where the finding sent it (PR body Acceptance notes; comment 7149072772: the relay can dispatch only on `main`). **The run itself has NOT happened and is the open landing condition, with the maintainer:**
